findings.title: Optimized paginator crashes on datetime audit logs
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to the order-by attribute, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this class with order_by="-datetime" whenever optimized_pagination=true and the caller is a superuser or has global access. Audit log rows are ordered by a datetime, not a number. On a non-empty first page, build_cursor calls get_item_key and raises TypeError because math.floor cannot accept a datetime. On any request that includes a cursor, build_queryset compares the timestamp column to that raw integer (DateTimePaginator converts via fromtimestamp and a multiplier; this class does not), which PostgreSQL rejects. The opt-in path therefore returns HTTP 500 for every organization that has audit log entries instead of a page of results.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets raise ValueError
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true (the audit log endpoint always passes True), OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with the raw negative cursor offset. Django's QuerySet rejects negative slice start or stop with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") before any SQL runs, so this branch never returns rows. Cursor.from_string accepts a negative offset, so a client that sends optimized_pagination=true and a cursor such as 0:-1:0 forces an HTTP 500. The comment that the ORM handles negative bounds, and that this reaches rows outside normal pagination limits, is false: the request errors, and the later trim check len(results) == offset + limit + extra would also be wrong for a negative offset if slicing were forced. The same false assumption was copied into BasePaginator.get_result, which now forwards a negative offset into queryset slicing for every is_prev cursor on all BasePaginator endpoints.

findings.title: No tests for the optimized audit-log pagination path
findings.body: The new optimized_pagination branch and OptimizedCursorPaginator have no tests. A request with audit log rows, or a cursor with a negative offset, 500s, which an endpoint test or a paginator unit test against a datetime queryset would have caught before merge. The shared BasePaginator slice change is also untested, so a regression there would hit every cursor-paginated endpoint, not just audit logs.
